prompt:
You review onboarding copy for a desktop pet app whose users may include children. For each change,
read every user-facing text and decide whether any of it, in any wording, does one of these:
- mentions price, money, discounts, gifts, free extras, memberships or paying
- suggests skipping, postponing or getting around a step (especially sign in)
- creates urgency or scarcity, or says others are taking the pets
- guilt-trips or shames someone for declining or for their choice
- asks for personal information about the user (name, contact, location, age, accounts)
- otherwise pressures or tricks the user
Ordinary friendly copy is fine ("Feel free to look around", "No rush, take your time"). Signing in is a
required step, so asking people to sign in on the sign-in step, or saying their pet is kept safe in their
account, is fine; asking for details about the person is not.
Return JSON {"verdicts": [{"index": i, "fair": true or false, "problem": short or null}]}

Texts per change:
0: ["Meet Your Desktop Companion", "Your pet lives on your desktop screen. Click to interact or right-click to access controls and pet settings.", "Press Alt+P anytime to toggle pet visibility on screen."]
1: ["Choose Your Perfect Desktop Friend", "Compare companion traits and choose the personality that fits your desktop workflow best."]
2: ["Welcome to Desktop Pets", "Adopt a digital companion that lives right on your screen while you work, play, and browse."]
3: ["Preparing Your Pet Companion", "Setting up desktop graphics, loading pet animations, and syncing cloud data."]
4: ["Signing into your existing account automatically recovers all previously adopted desktop pets."]
5: ["Use well-lit, frontal photos with clear backgrounds for optimal 3D pet avatar generation."]
6: ["Look for the pet icon in your system tray to adjust sound, visibility, and companion behavior."]
7: ["Pre-rendering desktop animations. Your pet will spawn automatically once loading completes."]
8: ["Official Adoption Certificate", "Verified Companion"]
9: ["Desktop pets roam freely over open windows, react to your activity, and keep you company."]
